LESSON: THROWING AND CATCHING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.2: Throwing and Catching
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Throwing and Catching, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Which direction can we throw and catch a ball during play? 2. How do we throw balls?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign vocabulary related to; perform throwing and catching activities (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Throwing and Catching in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify materials used to improvise a ball, (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Throwing and Catching in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. Improvise a ball from locally available materials, (

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. perform throwing and catching activities for skill acquisition of the game. (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Throwing and Catching in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Throwing and Catching together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner confidently throws and catches the ball while playing with peers.

• Learning to learn: The learner keenly follows the steps of knotting when making a ball.

Values:
• Unity: The learner cooperates with others when throwing and catching a ball.

• Love: The learner shares materials while making a ball.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environment conservation: The learner uses reusable locally available materials to improvise a ball.

Link to other learning areas:

• Environmental activities: The learner observes hygiene while using reusable locally available materials to improvise a ball.

• Language activities: The learner communicates with peers while throwing and catching.

Suggested learning resources:

Open safe quiet space, digital devices: laptops, tablets, phones, computers, assorted reusable materials, papers, polythene material, strings,

twines, mattress sponge, banana fibres, cotton wool, balls, field markers, relevant attire, reference books
